error list: LO PrivateCreator  - Error - Bad private owner value - element must be greater than or equal to 0x0010
fixes:
LO PrivateCreator  - Error - Bad private owner value - element must be greater than or equal to 0x0010 
***There will be a value in parenthesis preceeding the error, for example: (0x0005,0x0005) LO PrivateCreator  - Error - Bad private owner value - element must be greater than or equal to 0x0010***
%%% FIX IS -  (NOTE: this is the same fix for all private tags with this DCIODVFY error "Bad private owner value").
A. set_tag <(0010,0030)> <01021900> <> (Note: the set_tag edit does not have to be for this specific tag, any edit will "force" Posda to update the series associated with error. You can use any tag that is not important to the collection, such as the Accession Number DICOM tag; the value in the set_tag is not important as long as it is consistent with the VR).
delete_tag <(0005,0005)> <> <> (Note: replace the tag with the appropriate Private tag as indicated in the error e.g. 0x0005, 0x0005 is equivalent to Private tag 0005,0005)
B. Run BackgroundEditTP and import edits
C. If necessary, remember to fix the tag that was set in A, in this example, empty_tag <(0010,0030)> (Note: this must be the same tag that was set in A to "force" Posda to update the series.) %%%

NOTES: Need to check if the imaging data is Big Endian or Little Endian in Tag (0002,0010); Need to convert the Hex Tags to Decimal values using a Hex to Decimal Converter like the one found here: https://www.rapidtables.com/convert/number/hex-to-decimal.html;
The value you enter for the Hex value is dependent on whether your data is Big Endian or Little Endian.  If it is Big Endian you enter the 4 digit group first then the 4 digit element like 00540020, but if it is Little Endian, you enter the 4 digit element first then the 4 digit group like 00200054. The Decimal value returned is what is entered into the val1 of the set_tag command.
A. If tag (0054,0010) exists in the image header, set_tag (0028,0009)[0] <1048660> <> (where 1048660 is the decimal equivalent of 00100054 if the value in tag (0002,0010) is Little Endian or 5505040 if it is Big Endian) If the tag does not exist in the series, do not make this edit.

C. If tag (0054,0050) exists in the image header, set_tag (0028,0009)[2] <5242964> <> (where 5242964 is the decimal equivalent of 00500054 if the value in tag (0002,0010) is Little Endian or 5505104 if it is Big Endian). If the tag does not exist in the series, do not make this edit.
D. If tag (0054,0090) exists in the image header, set_tag (0028,0009)[3] <9437268> <> (where 9437268 is the decimal equivalent of 00900054 if the value in tag (0002,0010) is Little Endian or 5505168 if it is Big Endian). If the tag does not exist in the series, do not make this edit.

fixes:
Tag: (0054,0010) US 1-n Energy Window Vector : is conditional and is present when condition not satisfied : per NMMultiFrame module 
%%% FIX IS - If you see this error with the following:
Tag: (0028,0009) AT 1-n Frame Increment Pointer : Missing Tag : Type 1 Required Element : NMMultiFrame
Tag: (0054,0020) US 1-n Detector Vector : is conditional and is present when condition not satisfied : per NMMultiFrame module
Tag: (0054,0090) US 1-n Angular View Vector : is conditional and is present when condition not satisfied : per NMMultiFrame module
Tag: (0054,0050) US 1-n Rotation Vector : is conditional and is present when condition not satisfied : per NMMultiFrame module
You will need to:
NOTES: Need to check if the imaging data is Big Endian or Little Endian in Tag (0002,0010); Need to convert the Hex Tags to Decimal values using a Hex to Decimal Converter like  the one found here: https://www.rapidtables.com/convert/number/hex-to-decimal.html; 
The value you enter for the Hex value is dependent on whether your data is Big Endian or Little Endian.  If it is Big Endian you enter the 4 digit group first then the 4 digit element like 00540020, but if it is Little Endian, you enter the 4 digit element first then the 4 digit group like 00200054. The Decimal value returned is what is entered into the val1 of the set_tag command.
A.    If tag (0054,0010) exists in the image header, set_tag (0028,0009)[0] <1048660> <> (where 1048660 is the decimal equivalent of 00100054 if the value in tag (0002,0010) is Little Endian or 5505040 if it is Big Endian). Note: if (0054,0010) doesn't exist, do not make the edit.
B.   If tag (0054,0020) exists in the image header, set_tag (0028,0009)[1] <2097236> <> (where 2097236 is the decimal equivalent of 00200054 if the value in tag (0002,0010) is Little Endian or 5505056 if it is Big Endian) Note: if (0054,0020) doesn't exist, do not make the edit.
C.   If tag (0054,0050) exists in the image header, set_tag (0028,0009)[2] <5242964> <> (where 5242964 is the decimal equivalent of 00500054 if the value in tag (0002,0010) is Little Endian or 5505104 if it is Big Endian) Note: if (0054,0050) doesn't exist, do not make the edit.
D.    If tag (0054,0090) exists in the image header, set_tag (0028,0009)[3] <9437268> <> (where 9437268 is the decimal equivalent of 00900054 if the value in tag (0002,0010) is Little Endian or 5505168 if it is Big Endian) Note: if (0054,0090) doesn't exist, do not make the edit.

fixes:
Tag: (0054,0081) US 1 Number of Slices : is conditional and is present when condition not satisfied : per NMMultiFrame module %%% FIX IS - If this error is present with the following: 
Tag: (0054,0080) US 1-n Slice Vector : is conditional and is present when condition not satisfied : per NMMultiFrame module
Tag: (0028,0009) AT 1-n Frame Increment Pointer : Missing Tag : Type 1 Required Element : NMMultiFrame --> tag missing
Lowest value in vector is not one for Attribute (0x0054,0x0080) Slice Vector, but rather is 9
Specified number of vector values does not match actual values in vector for Attribute (0x0054,0x0081) Number of Slices, which has value 16, whereas the highest value found in (0x0054,0x0080) Slice Vector is 9
You will Multiple the values in tags (0028,0010) and (0028,0011) (Rows and columns respectively) by the value in tag (0028,0100) (Bits Allocated)/8 and if it equals the value in tag (7fe0,0010) and the value in tag (0028,0008) (Number of Frames) = 1 – ignore the error (but check with Bill if you see this error)
Example:Value in (0028,0010) aka Rows is 128
Value in (0028,0011) aka Columns is also 128
Value in (0028,0100) aka Bits Allocated is 16
128*128*16=262144
262144/8=32768
Value in (7fe0,0010) aka Pixel Data is 32768
Value in (0028,0008) aka Number of Frames is 1
